readMe.a: Account Field Health & Tech Debt Analysis — SBU

readMe.b: Identify which Account fields are genuinely in use and which are tech debt, using measured record-level population rather than estimates.
Live Salesforce metadata (object describe, Tooling FieldDefinition and CustomField) read directly from SBU production (Quilt Software / posnation) on 2026-10-02. No intermediate metadata export.

Created Date, Created By and Last Modified come live from Tooling CustomField. Flows, Formula Refs and Other Refs come live from Tooling MetadataComponentDependency; Layouts from parsing all 4 retrieved Account page layouts (Address sub-fields take the layout count of their parent Address field). Required? / Help Text / Description come from the live read. Required? = the field is not nillable. There is no August-style source catalogue for SBU Account, so the cross-check uses an independent server-side count (see caveat 5).
Full Bulk API 2.0 export of every Account record from SBU production. Every measure is an exact count over every Account, not a sample.
2014-05-04 to 2026-10-02 (record window; the 90d/365d windows use complete months only — see caveat 9)

422 of 427 live Account fields assessed. Id and the 4 compound Address parents (BillingAddress, Business_Address__c, Business__c, ShippingAddress) are excluded as non-data fields and listed on Not Assessable; their Address sub-fields ARE assessed. The 10 Long Text Area fields are assessed too, because the record export can test them for non-null.
Column "Age (days)", from the field's Created Date (Tooling CustomField). 69 fields (standard fields and the address sub-fields) have no creation date and show blank.
Column "% Populated (all records)" — measured across all 99,724 Accounts, not sampled.

Columns "Eligible Records (since creation)" and "% Populated Since Creation" restrict the denominator to Accounts created in or after the month the field was created. This is the fair measure: a field created in 2026 is not penalised for empty 2016 records.

"Adoption Lag (days)" is the gap between a field being created and the end of its first month of real use (>=1% of that month's Accounts). A long lag means the field sat unused after it was built; 4 fields waited over a year.
15 field(s) predate the first Account in the org and are measured across the whole window. Flagged in "Created Before Export Window".

72 fields are formulas or roll-up summaries. They compute a value on every record, so population, recency and trend are meaningless for them. Those three components score "n/a" and the total renormalises over information content, integration and documentation.
48 checkbox fields. A checkbox is populated on 100% of records by definition, so every measure here uses % TRUE instead — including recency and trend.

readMe.a: 4. New fields sit outside the score ladder
readMe.b: Fields under the grace period are banded "Too New - Provisional" rather than given a Healthy/Retire rating, because two components are structurally biased against them: Trend compares a 90-day window that predates the field, and Integration/Documentation lag behind field creation. Their score still shows, but as advisory only. Fields are also banded Provisional if they have too few eligible records to measure, whatever their age.

One column carries provenance: Custom (309), Standard (53) or Managed Package (60). Managed-package fields belong to an installed app (AVA_MAPPER, AVA_SFCLOUD, bofc, celigo_sfnsio, recurly_v2, ringcx_sf, ringdna, ringdna100, stripeGC) and cannot be deleted at all, so they are excluded from Retire Candidates and their Band shows "Managed Package" instead of a Healthy-to-Retire rating (the Health Score still shows, for reference only).

Weights, thresholds and bands are carried over unchanged from the SBU Case workbook (the same model used for the XBU Account workbook) so every object and business unit scores on the same scale. Every weight and threshold on the Scoring Model tab is a live input — edit it and this workbook recalculates.

Columns "Source Records Populated" and "Variance vs Source" compare the export count against an independent count run directly in the org (SELECT COUNT() FROM Account WHERE field != null, or = true for checkboxes), taken minutes apart on 2026-10-02. A small variance is Accounts created or edited between the two pulls, not an error. Source is blank for fields Salesforce cannot filter on (Long Text Area and similar). 411 of 411 comparable fields match exactly and the median absolute variance is 0.
IsDeleted was not used to filter; the Bulk export excludes soft-deleted records by default.

Distinct values are counted exactly over every Account from the export. Checkboxes show 1 when the box is ever TRUE and 0 when it never is. A distinct count of 0 means the field is never populated, not that cardinality is unknown.

The record measures cannot see reports, dashboards, or external integrations. The dependency graph (MetadataComponentDependency) does not track standard fields at all, so standard fields show only their Layouts count. A field can look dead here and still break something on deletion.

"% Populated Last 90d" is the three most recent complete months (2026-07 to 2026-09) and "% Populated Last 365d" the twelve most recent complete months (2025-10 to 2026-09), each restricted to Accounts eligible since the field's creation. Month-aligned windows keep the numerator and denominator consistent; records created in the partial month 2026-10 are excluded from both.
Every weight and threshold is an editable input (blue text, yellow fill). Change them and Field Health recalculates.
One row per assessed field: raw measures on the left, scored components and classification on the right.
Seeded with every retire candidate this analysis found. Add your own notes in the Notes column.
Custom, non-required fields past the grace period with no measurable current value.
Custom formula fields with no metadata references, or a single constant value.
Required fields not actually populated, fields adopted more than a year after creation, and fields with no help text or description.
A low score is a prompt to investigate, not an instruction to delete. Verify dependencies before removing any field.

"Effective Age (days)" (column AT) is now a live formula: the days between the Analysis as-of date (Scoring Model tab) and the older of the field's creation month and its first month carrying data. Formula and roll-up fields keep their metadata age, because they compute retroactively and would otherwise all look ancient; never-populated fields anchor to their creation month. It is reference information only: backfilled data can make a genuinely new field look years old, so the Band, Trend, Classification and Action formulas key the grace period on the literal "Age (days)" from the metadata Created Date. A field created within the grace period is always "Too New - Provisional" and can never be a retire candidate. The cost is that a deleted-and-redeployed long-standing field is parked provisional for one grace period — the safe direction of error.

Built 2026-10-02 against live SBU production using the same structure, columns, scoring formulas, classification and action rules as "Case Field Health Analysis SBU.xlsx" and "Account Field Health Analysis XBU.xlsx" (including the 2026-09-02 grace-period fix: the Too New check reads actual Age (days), not Effective Age). Differences from the Case build: records come from a full export rather than SOQL aggregates (so Long Text Areas are measurable), and references come from a live dependency crawl rather than a source catalogue.
